stem: Before a scheduled cycle of IV docetaxel, the nurse reviews a current CBC showing an absolute neutrophil count of 1,200 cells/mm³. Which action is appropriate?

options.A: Do not administer the docetaxel and notify the oncology team because the labeled neutrophil requirement for treatment has not been met.
options.B: Administer the docetaxel as scheduled because the total white blood cell count is more important than the absolute neutrophil count.
options.C: Give the docetaxel and repeat the CBC only if the client develops a fever after the infusion.
options.D: Independently reduce the docetaxel dose by half and administer it without contacting the prescribing team.

rationale: A is correct. The current DailyMed docetaxel label states not to administer docetaxel when the neutrophil count is below 1,500 cells/mm³ and directs frequent blood-count monitoring because neutropenia may be severe and result in infection. Section 5.3 also states not to retreat with subsequent cycles until neutrophils recover above 1,500 cells/mm³. An ANC of 1,200 cells/mm³ is below the labeled criterion, so the nurse should withhold administration and notify the oncology team. B and C disregard the explicit ANC-based safety criterion. D is outside the nurse's role because the nurse should not independently invent an antineoplastic dose reduction.
educational_objective: Use the current docetaxel label and a pre-treatment ANC to determine whether hematologic criteria for administration are met, withholding the drug and notifying the oncology team when the ANC is below 1,500 cells/mm³.
source_organization: DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_document_title: DOCETAXEL — docetaxel anhydrous injection, solution — Full Prescribing Information
source_locator: Highlights of Prescribing Information — neutropenia bullet; Section 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS — neutrophil counts <1,500 cells/mm³; Section 5.3 Hematologic Effects — frequent peripheral blood counts and no subsequent cycle until neutrophils recover >1,500 cells/mm³.
source_claim_supported: The current docetaxel label prohibits administration below ANC 1,500 cells/mm³, requires frequent blood-count monitoring, and sets recovery above 1,500 cells/mm³ before subsequent cycles.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — providing care related to medication and parenteral therapy administration; related activity statements include evaluating medication-order appropriateness/accuracy and preparing/administering medications using medication-administration rights.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the generic chemotherapy-CBC item into a docetaxel-specific medication-safety decision anchored to the current DailyMed label, eliminating an unsupported universal pre-cycle rule and remapping the construct to Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies.
audit_findings: DailyMed label currentness verified directly: page updated 2026-04-15 and revised 4/2026.
The ANC value 1,200 cells/mm³ is unambiguously below the label's 1,500 cells/mm³ administration threshold.
The key preserves nursing scope by withholding and notifying rather than independently changing the chemotherapy dose.
Distractors are realistic medication-safety errors and none is defensible under the label.
Independent adversarial review found no second answer, cueing, unsupported universal chemotherapy rule, threshold error, source-locator defect, or unresolved conflict.
